sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, status, reason, manager_id, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups for 'my leave requests' per employee; manager_id: frequent lookups for pending approvals assigned to a manager; status: filtering by status (pending/approved/rejected) for approval queues and dashboards; leave_type: filtering by leave type for balance calculations and reporting; created_at: ordering and date-range queries for history views
table leave_types | fields: id, name, description, max_days_per_year, requires_approval, created_at | pk: id | indexes: name: unique lookup by leave type name for policy enforcement and validation

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, year, total_days, used_days, pending_days, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups for an employee's balance summary; leave_type_id: filtering balances by leave type; (employee_id, leave_type_id): composite lookup for 'how many annual leave days does employee X have left' — the most common query pattern; (employee_id, year): year-scoped balance queries per employee

table audit_log | fields: id, employee_id, leave_request_id, action, previous_state, new_state, performed_by, created_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_request_id -> leave_requests.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups of audit trail by employee; leave_request_id: lookups of audit trail for a specific leave request; action: filtering by action type (created/approved/rejected/cancelled); created_at: chronological ordering for audit views

methods: findByEmployeeId(employeeId: string, filters?: { status?: string; leaveType?: string; fromDate?: Date; toDate?: Date }): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
findByManagerId(managerId: string, filters?: { status?: string }): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
updateStatus(id: string, status: string, updatedBy: string): Promise<LeaveRequest>
countByEmployeeAndTypeAndDateRange(employeeId: string, leaveTypeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date): Promise<number>
findByEmployeeIdAndLeaveTypeIdAndYear(employeeId: string, leaveTypeId: string, year: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>
upsertBalance(employeeId: string, leaveTypeId: string, year: number, deltaUsed: number, deltaPending: number): Promise<LeaveBalance>

data_notes: Four conceptual tables defined: leave_requests (core entity with employee/manager FK, status lifecycle), leave_types (reference data for annual/sick/emergency), leave_balances (per-employee per-type per-year tracking with used_days and pending_days), and audit_log (GP-002 compliance — every state change recorded). Four repository interfaces with concrete pg Pool implementations: ILeaveRequestRepository/PgLeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveTypeRepository/PgLeaveTypeRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository/PgLeaveBalanceRepository, IAuditLogRepository/PgAuditLogRepository. All backings use the existing shared db connection (src/shared/db/connection.ts). Index rationale covers the primary access patterns: employee-scoped lookups, manager approval queues, status filtering, leave-type filtering, composite employee+type+year balance queries, and chronological audit trails.
